analysis: Documentation-only change in docs/architecture/security/identity-binding.md: bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) to 2026-10-14 and extends the SE P-256 signing key row (head line 52) to say a dev build uses label io.darkbloom.dev.provider.attestation-signing.v2 in the same access group SLDQ2GJ6TL.io.darkbloom.provider, giving it a separate SE identity. No code, protocol, or policy changed. Relevant: A-002, T-035, T-034, TB-009, TB-011. Assumptions for later passes: (1) the Swift PersistentEnclaveKey.swift implementation, which is not in this PR, must actually select the dev label only for dev builds; the doc claim is unverified. (2) The coordinator's binary-hash and code-qualification policy (T-034, T-054) must still prevent a dev-signed or unqualified build from gaining serving trust; the SE key is only a signing identity, and App Attest and release qualification still gate serving. (3) Dev and prod keys share an access group, so isolation is by label only, not by keychain boundary. That is a documented fact rather than a regression, and the head file is truncated in the excerpt (it ends at line 239), so the tail of the file is unexamined; the base tail was visible but is unchanged by the patch. No security regression, new attack surface, or invalidated threat-model assumption found.
